# What distinguishes responders from non-responders?

::: {.callout-warning}
The tables on this page name households — local only.
:::

Cross-cuts of the appealed households, then two named lists: the biggest
responses, and the higher-tier prior donors who did **not** respond.

```{python}
#| label: setup-who
import pandas as pd
from hh.clean.accounts import clean_accounts
from hh.clean.donations import clean_donations
from hh.external.notes import load_boyd_notes
from hh.io import read_parquet
from hh.analytics.appeal import last_gift_year_totals
from hh.viz import money, pct

t = read_parquet("processed", "appeal_households.parquet")
ap = t[t["appealed"]].copy()

n_big_silent = int((ap["prior_donor"] & ~ap["responded"]).sum())
big_total = ap.loc[ap["prior_donor"] & ~ap["responded"], "prior_lifetime_amount"].sum()
n_5k_silent = int(
    (ap["prior_donor"] & ~ap["responded"] & (ap["prior_lifetime_amount"] >= 5000)).sum()
)
top_dollars = ap.nlargest(25, "afd_amount")["afd_amount"].sum()
top_share = top_dollars / ap["afd_amount"].sum()

# last-gift-year totals and Don's stewardship notes, shared with the workbook export
donations = clean_donations(accounts=clean_accounts())
last_yr = last_gift_year_totals(donations)
notes = load_boyd_notes()


def town_with_state(row) -> str:
    """Town, with the state abbreviation appended when it is not New York."""
    city = "" if pd.isna(row["city"]) else str(row["city"]).strip()
    state = "" if pd.isna(row["state_province"]) else str(row["state_province"]).strip()
    if not city:
        return state if state and state != "NY" else ""
    return f"{city}, {state}" if state and state != "NY" else city
```

## Prior giving × engagement

Cells show appealed households and, in parentheses, the share that responded.

```{python}
cross = pd.crosstab(
    ap["prior_donor"].map({True: "prior donor", False: "never gave"}),
    ap["eng_profile"],
)
rates = pd.crosstab(
    ap["prior_donor"].map({True: "prior donor", False: "never gave"}),
    ap["eng_profile"],
    values=ap["responded"],
    aggfunc="mean",
)
(cross.astype(str) + " (" + rates.map(pct) + ")").rename_axis(index=None).rename_axis(
    columns="engagement"
)
```

## Biggest responses

The top `{python} f"{25:,}"` responding households gave `{python} money(top_dollars)`
— `{python} pct(top_share)` of all appeal-window dollars from appealed households.

```{python}
cols = ["name", "appeal_segment", "prior_size_tier", "afd_n_gifts", "afd_amount", "city"]
top = ap[ap["responded"]].nlargest(25, "afd_amount")[cols].reset_index(drop=True)
top = top.rename(
    columns={
        "name": "household", "appeal_segment": "segment", "prior_size_tier": "prior tier",
        "afd_n_gifts": "gifts", "afd_amount": "appeal gifts", "city": "town",
    }
)
top["appeal gifts"] = top["appeal gifts"].map(money)
top
```

## Prior $1,000+ households that did not respond

In total, `{python} f"{n_big_silent:,}"` prior-donor households with
`{python} money(big_total)` of lifetime giving before the appeal did not respond —
including `{python} f"{n_5k_silent}"` in the `$5,000+` lifetime tier. The 25 largest
of those (*last-gift-yr $* = what the household gave in the calendar year of its
most recent pre-appeal gift; *note* = Don's stewardship notes, kept in the local
`data/30_external/boyd-notes.yaml`):

```{python}
big_silent = ap[
    ap["prior_donor"] & ~ap["responded"] & (ap["prior_lifetime_amount"] >= 1000)
].nlargest(25, "prior_lifetime_amount")
big_silent = big_silent.merge(last_yr, on="id", how="left")

tbl = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "household": big_silent["name"],
        "segment": big_silent["appeal_segment"],
        "lifetime before appeal": big_silent["prior_lifetime_amount"].map(money),
        "last gift": big_silent["prior_last_gift"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
        "last-gift-yr $": big_silent["last_gift_year_total"].map(
            lambda v: money(v) if pd.notna(v) else "—"
        ),
        "engagement": big_silent["eng_profile"],
        "town": big_silent.apply(town_with_state, axis=1),
        "note": big_silent["id"].astype(str).map(notes),
    }
).reset_index(drop=True)
tbl
```

## Staff notes on the mailing list

Notes typed into the workbook next to recipients — returned mail, deceased
flags, sustaining-donor markers.

```{python}
rec = read_parquet("processed", "appeal_recipients.parquet")
notes = rec[rec["staff_notes"].notna()][
    ["workbook_name", "source_sheet", "appeal_gift_recorded", "staff_notes"]
].reset_index(drop=True)
notes = notes.rename(
    columns={
        "workbook_name": "household", "source_sheet": "sheet",
        "appeal_gift_recorded": "recorded gift", "staff_notes": "note",
    }
)
notes["recorded gift"] = notes["recorded gift"].map(money)
notes
```
